questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: First Nations peoples have a deep connection to the land, waters and sky around them. What word do they use for this place they belong to and care for?
questions.explanation: First Nations peoples use the word Country for the land, waters and sky they belong to and look after.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Many First Nations groups live across Australia. What does each group have of its own?
choices: The same language as all other groups
Its own language, stories and customs
questions.explanation: There are many different First Nations groups. Each has its own language, stories and customs.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: All First Nations peoples in Australia speak the same language.
questions.explanation: There are many First Nations groups, and they speak many different languages.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: The First Fleet arrived in 1788. Why did Britain set up a colony in Australia?
choices: To build a new capital city
To send convicts because the prisons were full
questions.explanation: British prisons were overcrowded. Britain wanted a new place to send convicts.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Britain used to send convicts to America. Then America became independent. What did Britain need to find?
choices: A new place to send convicts
questions.explanation: Britain could no longer send convicts to America. So it chose Australia as a new place.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: What was a convict on the First Fleet?
choices: A soldier who guarded the ships
A farmer who came to buy land
A person sent far away as punishment for a crime
questions.explanation: Convicts were people found guilty of crimes. They were sent to the colony as punishment.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Arthur Phillip sailed with the First Fleet. What was his job in the new colony?
choices: Governor in charge of the colony
questions.explanation: Arthur Phillip was the first governor. He was the official in charge of the colony.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Marines sailed with the First Fleet. What was their main job in the colony?
choices: Guarding the convicts and keeping order
questions.explanation: Marines were soldiers. They guarded the convicts and kept order in the colony.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Settlers built farms and towns near Sydney Cove. What often happened to First Nations peoples who lived there?
choices: They were given the new farms
They were cut off from their land and food sources
questions.explanation: Settlers took over land. Many First Nations people lost access to their food, water and special places.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: The people on the First Fleet brought illnesses that were new to Australia. What happened to many First Nations people?
choices: They became sick, and many died
questions.explanation: First Nations peoples had no protection from these new illnesses, so many became very sick and died.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Why is a river important to the animals living near it in the Australian bush?
choices: It gives them drinking water and food
It helps them tell the time
questions.explanation: Animals need water to drink. Rivers also give them plants and other food.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Africa is another continent. Why do many animals gather at a waterhole on the African savanna?
questions.explanation: The savanna can be very dry. Animals gather at waterholes to drink.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Which of these is a resource that cannot be replaced once it is used up?
questions.explanation: Coal took millions of years to form. We cannot make more in our lifetime, but wind and sunshine keep coming.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: How have First Nations peoples looked after Country for thousands of years?
choices: By taking as much as they can
By caring for it and only taking what is needed
By leaving it and never visiting
questions.explanation: First Nations peoples have a duty to care for Country. They take only what they need so it stays healthy.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Which of these is a law, not just a school or family rule?
choices: Stopping at a red traffic light
questions.explanation: Laws are made by governments for everyone. Breaking the red light law can lead to a fine.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Why do we have laws in Australia?
choices: To keep people safe and treat them fairly
So only some people are allowed to drive
questions.explanation: Laws help keep people safe and make sure everyone is treated fairly.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Which of these jobs does your local council usually do?
choices: Collecting rubbish bins and looking after parks
questions.explanation: Local councils look after local things like rubbish collection, parks and local roads.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Sam wants to support the local library. Which action helps most?
choices: Borrowing books and returning them on time
questions.explanation: Using the library and looking after its books helps the service keep running for everyone.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Lena's family goes to church every Sunday. What kind of group does this show she belongs to?
questions.explanation: People who share a faith and worship together are part of a religious group.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Groups we belong to, like family, culture and teams, help shape our identity. What is identity?
choices: Who you are and what makes you, you
questions.explanation: Identity is who you are. The groups you belong to help make you who you are.
